Tone: The FOMC’s 25 bp cut alongside “solid” activity, easing-but-still-tight labor markets, and inflation progress is modestly positive. However, SLOOS details temper this: banks report tightened C&I standards and weaker demand among small and middle‑market firms; CRE standards remain tight (with large banks unchanged for CLD but somewhat easier for multifamily); subprime consumer credit is tighter while RRE and HELOC standards are largely unchanged; foreign banks report stronger C&I demand, but domestic demand looks softer. Combined with ongoing QT and money market facility settings at the floor, the stance is balanced with a cautious tilt. Net: slightly positive macro, constrained by tighter/softer credit backdrop.
